access.title: Access levels and RMF
access.snippet: The Google Ads API is free to use; there are no charges for using the Google Ads API at Explorer access, Basic access, or Standard access levels. However, if you are subject to [Required Minimum Functionality (RMF)](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/api-policy/rmf), the API Review Team audits your tool for compliance. If the audit results in a finding of non-compliance, you may be required to pay [non-compliance fees](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/api-policy/non-compliance-fee).

access.title: Google Ads API onboarding guide
access.snippet:
The developer token uniquely identifies your application to the Google Ads API and controls your call volume access tier.
### Steps to apply
1. Sign in to your **Google Ads Manager Account**.
2. Navigate to **Tools and settings > Setup > API Center** (or **Admin > API Center**).
3. Fill out the developer details form and agree to the API Terms of Service.
4. Submit your application.
### Access levels
- **Pending Approval:** Newly created tokens immediately receive a "Pending" status. You can use a pending token to connect to **Test Accounts** immediately, but it won't work against production accounts.
- **Basic Access:** Allows up to 15,000 API operations per day once approved.
- **Standard Access:** Unlimited daily API operations for applications that meet the Required Minimum Functionality (RMF).

- **Developer Token Usage:** Do **not** apply for a developer token from your Test Manager Account. Always use the pending or approved developer token from your **Production Manager Account**.

### Pricing and billing
- **No API Fees:** Creating a Google Cloud project, enabling the Google Ads API, and generating OAuth 2.0 credentials is **100% free**. Google does not charge any fees for calling or using the Google Ads API itself.
- **Other Cloud Resources:** You will only incur Google Cloud fees if you actively use other billable Google Cloud services (such as Compute Engine, Cloud Run, or BigQuery) beyond their Free Tier limits to host your application or store your ad data.

access.title: Google Ads API: Access Levels, Costs and Setup (2026)
access.snippet:
The Google Ads API lets you read account data and change campaigns programmatically, whether from your own scripts or from a workflow tool like [Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com), and it **costs nothing per call**.
It needs three things before a request works: a developer token, OAuth credentials and a Google Ads account.
Google issues the approval for the token, and **no route around that exists**. Checked against Google's developer documentation on 1 Nov 2026.

You will not be billed per call: Google doesn't charge for Google Ads API requests. The price of a request is zero.
That's not the same as "free of limits": usage is still governed by quotas and access levels tied to your developer token. A call can fail on a quota without ever costing you money.
When a request is rejected, the error response says which limit you hit, and that's the part worth reading closely.

| Item | Where you get it | Who issues it | What fails without it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Developer token | Google Ads API Center in a manager account | Google, after review | Every request is rejected |
| OAuth credentials | Google Cloud project, plus a user consent step | Google Cloud, you configure them | Requests fail authentication |
| Google Ads account | Google Ads sign-up | Google Ads, you own the account | No data to query or change |
| Cost per call | Not applicable | Not applicable | $0 |
*Prices and plan limits checked against [docs.claude.com](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/about-claude/models/overview) and [claude.com](https://claude.com/pricing) and [openai.com](https://openai.com/chatgpt/pricing) and [gemini.google](https://gemini.google/subscriptions) on October 31, 2026.*

| Access level | Daily operations | Account reach | Approval | Review time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Test | no figure published | Test accounts only | None beyond the token | no figure published |
| Explorer | 2,880 | Production accounts | Application reviewed by Google | no figure published |
| Basic | 15,000 | Production accounts | Application reviewed by Google | no figure published |
| Standard | no figure published | Production accounts | Application reviewed by Google | no figure published |

The free plan is $0 with 1,000 credits a month and unlimited flows, so the same weekly flow fits there too.

mcp.title: Google Ads MCP server: Developer integration guide
mcp.snippet:
The **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** is an open standard that lets large language models (LLMs) securely interact with external data and applications. The **Google Ads MCP server** provides a standardized bridge to the Google Ads API. It lets AI agents retrieve and analyze account data, create assets, upload videos, and manage labels by using natural language.

### Key specifications
- **Protocol:** MCP (Model Context Protocol)
- **Mode:** Read and partial mutate (asset creation, video uploads, and label management with propose-and-confirm validation, or configurable read-only mode)
- **Language:** Python 3.10 or later
- **Transport:** Standard input/output (`stdio`) or Streamable HTTP (`streamable-http` on Cloud Run)
- **Authentication:** Application Default Credentials (OAuth 2.0 user credentials or service account) for local `stdio`, or OAuth 2.0 Web application credentials for remote HTTP
### How the interaction loop works
1. **Request:** You submit a prompt such as *"How is my campaign performance this week?"* or *"Create a callout asset for our summer sale"*.
2. **Discovery:** The LLM inspects its available tools and resources and selects a matching `google-ads-mcp` tool.
3. **Execution or dry-run validation:** Read tools query the Google Ads API directly. Mutate tools first run in propose mode (`validate_only=True`) to validate inputs without committing changes (see Propose-and-confirm safety workflow).
4. **Context injection:** The MCP server returns structured query results, or proposed `change_items` entries and a verification `checksum` digest, to the LLM's context window.
5. **Response and confirmation:** The LLM presents an answer or asks you to confirm the proposed changes. After you approve, the LLM calls the mutate tool again with `validate_only=False` and the matching `checksum` value to commit the change.

mcp.snippet:
# Google Ads MCP Server
This repo contains the source code for running an
[MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that interacts with the
[Google Ads API](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api).
## Tools
The server uses the
[Google Ads API](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/latest/overview)
to provide several
[Tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools) and [Resources](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools) for use with LLMs and AI agents.
### Tools available
- `search`: Retrieves information about the Google Ads account using GAQL.
- `get_resource_metadata`: Retrieves metadata about a Google Ads API resource type, for example "campaign". This is useful to understand the structure of the data and what fields are available for querying.
- `list_accessible_customers`: Returns IDs of customers directly accessible
by the user authenticating the call.
- `create_asset`: Creates Google Ads assets (`TEXT`, `IMAGE`, `YOUTUBE_VIDEO`, `SITELINK`, `CALLOUT`, `STRUCTURED_SNIPPET`, and other asset types via `extra_params`). Note: `image_asset_path` is supported in local `stdio` mode only; use base64 `image_asset_data` for remote HTTP deployments.
- `upload_video_asset`: Uploads a local video file to YouTube via the Google Ads API using a background task so it can be referenced by video assets (supported in local `stdio` mode only).
- `manage_labels`: Creates, updates, and removes account labels.
- `manage_label_associations`: Creates and removes label associations on `CAMPAIGN`, `CUSTOMER`, `AD_GROUP`, and `AD_GROUP_CRITERION` resources.

The Google Ads MCP server uses `tools_config.yaml` to let you selectively enable or disable individual tools or tool categories (namespaces) and customize their namespace prefixes.
A default `tools_config.yaml` with all tools enabled is bundled with the package, so the server works out of the box with no extra setup. For strictly read-only deployments, set `labels: false` and `assets: false` in your `tools_config.yaml`.

Once deployed, update your MCP client configuration (refer to the docs at [https://antigravity.google/docs/mcp](https://antigravity.google/docs/mcp)) to use the Cloud Run URL.
```json
{
"mcpServers": {
"google-ads-mcp": {
"httpUrl": "https://your-cloud-run-url.a.run.app/mcp"
}
}
}
```

mcp.snippet:
The Google Ads MCP Server is an implementation of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) that enables Large Language Models (LLMs), such as Gemini, to interact directly with the Google Ads API.
Note
This is NOT an officially supported Google product. It is mainly for experimental purposes and not intended for production use. Consider using the official [Google Ads MCP Server](https://github.com/google-ads/google-ads-mcp-python) instead.

This project uses [`uv`](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv) for dependency management.
Install `uv` and then run the following command to install the required Python packages:
```
uv pip sync
```
### 2. Configure Google Ads credentials
This tool requires you to have a `google-ads.yaml` file with your Google Ads API credentials. By default, the application will look for this file in your home directory.
If you don't have one, you can generate it by running the following example from the `google-ads-python` library: [authentication example](https://github.com/googleads/google-ads-python/blob/main/examples/authentication/generate_user_credentials.py)

### Read-Only Tools (Always Available)
- **GAQL Execution**: Query Google Ads data using GAQL.
- **Account Management**: List accessible accounts.
- **Documentation**: Access documentation for GAQL and reporting views.
### Mutation Tools (Disabled by Default)
To enable these tools, set `ADS_MCP_ENABLE_MUTATIONS=true`.
- **Campaign Budgets**: Create campaign budgets.
- **Campaigns**: Create campaigns.
- **Ad Groups**: Create ad groups.
- **Ads**: Create ads.
- **Criteria**: Create criteria (e.g., keywords).

# Google Ads MCP Server
An [MCP (Model Context Protocol)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that enables LLMs and AI agents to query and manage [Google Ads](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api) accounts.

The Google Ads MCP Server exposes [MCP Tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools) and [MCP Resources](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/resources) backed by the [Google Ads API](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/latest/overview). It supports:
- **Read & reporting workflows**: GAQL queries, accessible customer discovery, resource field metadata, and API reference resources.
- **Guarded account mutations**: Asset creation, video uploads, and label management protected by a two-step **Propose & Confirm** workflow.
- **Flexible deployment**: Run locally over `stdio` with Application Default Credentials, or over **Streamable HTTP** with FastMCP's OAuth proxy and structured audit logging.
> **Notes:**
>
> - Connecting an LLM or agent to this server exposes your accessible Google Ads account data to that client.
> - API calls made by this server include an MCP telemetry header used by Google to collect usage statistics and improve the product.
> - Report bugs or feature requests on the [GitHub issue tracker](https://github.com/googleads/google-ads-mcp/issues).
---
## Quickstart & Setup
### 1. Prerequisites
1. **Python & `pipx`** (for local non-container setups): Python 3.11+ and [`pipx`](https://pipx.pypa.io/stable/#install-pipx). To run a specific released version from PyPI:
```
pipx run --spec "google-ads-mcp==X.Y.Z" google-ads-mcp
```
2. **Google Cloud Project**: Enable the [Google Ads API](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/googleads.googleapis.com) in your Google Cloud project ([how to enable APIs](https://support.google.com/googleapi/answer/6158841)).
### 2. Choose an Authentication Mode
The server supports two authentication and transport modes out of the box:
| Mode | Transport | Best For |
|---|---|---|
| **Mode A: Application Default Credentials (ADC)** | `stdio` | Single-user local CLI/IDE agents where the MCP client spawns the server directly. |
| **Mode B: FastMCP OAuth Proxy** | `streamable-http` | Shared/remote deployments or local containers where server credentials stay isolated from MCP client configs. |

#### Connecting via Streamable HTTP (Mode B — Recommended for Shared or Container Setups)

mcp.title: Google Ads MCP server: Developer integration guide
mcp.snippet:
The **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** is an open standard that enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to securely interact with external data and applications. The **Google Ads MCP server** provides a standardized bridge to the Google Ads API, which lets AI agents analyze and retrieve campaign data using natural language.

### Key specifications
- **Protocol:** MCP (Model Context Protocol)
- **Mode:** **Read-only** (current release)
- **Language:** Python
- **Transport:** Standard input/output (`stdio`)
- **Authentication:** OAuth 2.0 or service account
### How the interaction loop works
1. **Request:** A user submits a query such as *"How is my campaign performance this week?"*.
2. **Discovery:** The LLM inspects its available tools and identifies the `google-ads-mcp` search capabilities.
3. **Execution:** The MCP server executes the underlying Python logic to query the Google Ads API.
4. **Context injection:** Structured results are returned to the LLM's context window.
5. **Response:** The LLM synthesizes the data into a human-readable answer.

Before configuration, ensure you have the following credentials from the [Google Ads Developer console](/google-ads/api/docs/get-started/introduction):
- **Developer token:** Your unique 22-character access string.
- **Project ID:** Your Google Cloud project identifier.
- **OAuth credentials:** Either an OAuth2 Client ID/Client secret pair, or a set of [application default credentials](//docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/application-default-credentials).
### Configuration
To integrate the server into an MCP-compatible host, add the following entry to your host's MCP configuration file, such as `settings.json`. Consult your host's documentation for the exact location and filename of this configuration.
JSON
```
{ "mcpServers" : { "google-ads-mcp" : { "command" : "pipx" , "args" : [ "run" , "--spec" , "git+https://github.com/googleads/google-ads-mcp.git" , "google-ads-mcp" ], "env" : { "GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID" : "YOUR_PROJECT_ID" , "GOOGLE_ADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN" : "YOUR_DEVELOPER_TOKEN" } } } }
```

mcp.snippet:
The **Google Ads MCP Server** is a Python implementation of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) that bridges Large Language Models (LLMs), such as Gemini, with the Google Ads API. It allows users to interact with their Google Ads accounts using natural language queries to retrieve campaigns, metrics, and other data.
It exposes several MCP tools and resources:
- **Tools:**
- `execute_gaql`: Execute Google Ads Query Language queries.
- `list_accessible_accounts`: List accessible customer IDs.
- `get_gaql_doc`: Retrieve GAQL grammar documentation.
- `get_reporting_view_doc`: Retrieve documentation for specific reporting views (e.g., campaign, ad_group).
- **Resources:**
- `resource://Google_Ads_Query_Language`: GAQL guide.
- `resource://Google_Ads_API_Reporting_Views`: Overview of reporting views.
- `resource://views/{view}`: Detailed metadata for specific views.
## Tech Stack
- **Language:** Python 3.12+
- **Package Manager:** `uv`
- **Key Libraries:**
- `fastmcp`: For building the MCP server.
- `google-ads`: Official Google Ads API client.
- `mcp`: Core MCP library.
- `pytest`: Testing framework.
